Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and the screenshot.

Sorry about the confusion. We recently saw a few customers hit a similar edge case when their browser timezone and IP-derived timezone differ (common when people use corporate VPNs). Calendly/Chili Piper will usually use the browser timezone, but the calendar that gets added can sometimes end up in the account default timezone depending on the client.

I can do two things right away:
- Send a manual .ics for 24 Nov 14:00 CET (I'll attach it to this thread).
- Create a fallback meeting in Google Calendar with the event timezone explicitly set to Europe/Paris so it can't be interpreted incorrectly.

Marissa — looping you in to note FintechCo is buyer-side (budget conversation later).

Olivia — will send the ICS and a one-click Google Meet link. If that looks good, accept and we'll lock it.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt

Quick note — we've seen DST-related offsets bite a few EU->US cross-region bookings this fall. Two tips that help: force UTC in the Calendly link (append ?tz=UTC) or generate the invite from Google Calendar and set the event timezone explicitly (Europe/Paris or Europe/Berlin depending on customer).

If you want, I can make a UTC-locked meeting link for this account so they don't have to worry about local browser settings.
